name: OpenAPI Documentation
description: Document REST APIs with OpenAPI (Swagger) specifications for consistency, testing, and client generation.
content:
# OpenAPI Documentation Rules

- Define an OpenAPI 3.1 spec for every REST API — it is the contract between frontend and backend
- Document every endpoint with path, method, summary, description, and operationId
- Define request bodies with JSON Schema — include required fields, types, formats, and examples
- Document all response codes — 200, 201, 400, 401, 403, 404, 422, 500 with schema and example for each
- Use `$ref` for reusable schemas — define models in `components/schemas` and reference them in endpoints
- Include authentication requirements — define security schemes (Bearer, API Key, OAuth2) and apply them per endpoint
- Add `example` values to every property — examples make the spec usable without reading descriptions
- Use `tags` to group related endpoints — `Users`, `Products`, `Orders` for logical organization
- Keep the spec in sync with the implementation — generate it from code annotations or validate code against the spec in CI
- Use Swagger UI or Redoc to serve interactive documentation — developers should be able to try endpoints from the docs
- Generate client SDKs from the spec — `openapi-generator` produces typed clients for TypeScript, Python, Go, and more
- Version your API in the spec — `info.version` should match your API version, update it with breaking changes
